lines.text: Your agent is great at code. But it has no idea your task list, your notes, or your teammates exist.
So you paste the task, paste the notes, and paste the rules, again and again, every session.
Add one line of config, and Agent R Q plugs into the agent over M C P, the Model Context Protocol.
The agent gets seven native tools, which show up beside the ones it already has.
Tasks and replies. The agent picks up its own work, and answers you when it is done.
Memory keeps what it learned, and skills hold the playbooks, so lessons stick between sessions.
Pano docs and shared websites give it the same pages your team reads.
Even a help tool that explains every action, so nobody has to write a manual.
Now the agent picks up its own tasks, replies when it is stuck, and saves what it learned.
You just watch the board move, and step in only when it needs a human decision.
Risky actions still wait for your approval, so connecting an agent never costs you control.
What would you let your agents do on their own? Share it, or connect one at Agent R Q dot com.
